title: Hambone Inn, 1952, and Eaton's Club flyers
summary: A photo shows him on sax at the Hambone Inn in Mississippi with Dan Seals, plus flyers for Slidell and Eaton's Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: We've got a picture from the Hambone Inn. It says, it's you on saxophone, F.J. Curley-Lazana. And there's a clarinet in the picture, too. That's his. And one of the guitar players is named Bobby.

Yeah, that was Bobby. We showed it to you a long time ago. We didn't get Bobby's last name. We didn't get the other guitar player. Didn't get his last name? Dan Seals, who was the owner of the Hambone Possible. Seals, the owner. He played an officer, too. He was the owner. He was a bass player. Yeah, he played bass and he played guitar, too. Yeah. Dan played bass and guitar. And what's the most?
This is Hambone Inn, 1952. Hansborough, Mississippi. Pass Road.
That's Back Road. They call it Pass Road the old Back Road.

And Bosco's of Slidell must have been about the same time, he says. Right. It was in to Saturday Night 3. And that's the best love club also comes in at the same time. Eaton's Club also comes in about the same time. Dancing on Sundays, 2 to 8 p.m. Music by the Blue Moves. Wow. Yeah, that was another band. Commission, 75 cents. Tell your friends. Thanks, Eaton.
You know why I wasn't there.
G-A-R-R-I-G-A. That's how it was, 65 cents.
What's the name? G-A-R-R-I-G-A. Garriga. Garriga. G-A-R-R-I-G-A. Garriga. I'm not good on these names. But you didn't come back into music until about 1950 and so on. Late years.
